name: Livermore Youth Council (LYC)
what_you_do: Members speak for Livermore youth to the City Council, the park district (LARPD) and the school district (LVJUSD). They plan events, promote youth programs and community service, and review City Council agendas.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in Livermore or go to a school in Livermore. The council has 20 members.
duration: A new term starts each school year. Members serve 2-year terms, then say if they want to keep serving. Meetings are the first Monday of each month at 7 p.m., plus subcommittee meetings and events.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application was due July 31, 2026 at 6 p.m., with interviews in August. 2027-28 dates are not posted yet. Expect a summer deadline again.
how_to_apply: Fill out the paper application. It asks three short questions: why you want to join, your civic or community activities, and anything else about you. A parent or guardian must sign. Turn it in at the Civic Center Library Information Desk or email it to njbrumley@livermoreca.gov. Selected applicants get an interview.
notes: This replaces the older Livermore Area Youth Advisory Commission (LAYAC) card. The city's youth page now calls the group the Livermore Youth Council and links to the library page. Three absences in one school year count as quitting. Members are picked through an application review and interview by adult liaisons and some LYC members; the City liaison makes the final choice. Program supervisor: Nathan Brumley, Assistant Library Director, 925-373-5572. The page fetches were done with firecrawl because livermoreca.gov blocks plain fetches.
